title: Point covers of etale scheme charts are fppf-local lifting families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $Y$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], $I$ any index type, and $V_i$ schemes with representable etale maps $v_i:h_{V_i}\to Y$. Then the family is jointly surjective on point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] if and only if, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every $a:h_T\to Y$, the sieve generated by maps $k:U\to T$ admitting $i\in I$ and $b:U\to V_i$ with $h_k\mathbin{\gg}a=h_b\mathbin{\gg}v_i$ covers $T$ in the big fppf topology over $S$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. No finiteness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), with definition-etale-covering and spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU; residue-field verification of the local lifting characterization.

proof.text: Represent each chart base change to an arbitrary T by an etale scheme U_i -> T using the definition of representable etale map. Apply point-class lifting to the image under a of the residue-field point of each x in T. The compatible lifts give a morphism Spec L -> U_i above x, so the scheme maps U_i -> T are jointly surjective.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), with definition-etale-covering and spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU; residue-field verification of the local lifting characterization.

proof.text: The jointly surjective etale scheme family is fppf. Its generated covering sieve is contained in the displayed factorization sieve: pull back the first projection of each cartesian square and use its commutativity. Thus the displayed sieve covers.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), with definition-etale-covering and spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU; residue-field verification of the local lifting characterization.

proof.text: Conversely apply the sieve condition to Spec K -> Y. A covering fppf sieve has a member with a point above the unique point of Spec K. Restrict to that point's residue field L. The resulting map Spec L -> Spec K is induced by its unique ring map K -> L. Downward closure of the factorization condition supplies a chart lift of the restricted section. This is precisely the required point-class lift.

lean.statement:
theorem isJointlySurjective_iff_fppf_lifting
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {Y : AlgebraicSpace S} {I : Type v}
    (V : I → Y.EtaleSite) :
    IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (V i).obj.hom) ↔
      ∀ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y.obj.obj),
        Sieve.generate (fun (U : Over S) (k : U ⟶ T) ↦
          ∃ (i : I) (b : U ⟶ (V i).obj.left),
            yoneda.map k ≫ a = yoneda.map b ≫ (V i).obj.hom) ∈
              (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) T
